name: Respiratory variants & flu
value: US flu admissions 9,584 (to 7 Nov); severity low
summary: Flu seasons start early in the US and UK; US admissions over seven times last year's level, CDC still rates severity low
state: CDC reported 9,584 flu hospital admissions in the week to 7 Nov, more than seven times the same week last season, with seven jurisdictions at high or very high activity, up from two; it rates severity as low for all ages (CDC; Becker's Hospital Review, 16 Nov). UKHSA surveillance since early November shows flu admissions in England rising earlier than usual (UKHSA). Searches on 25 Nov found no new WHO variant designation and no health systems reported as strained, so Watch holds.
for_you: The NHS offers free flu and COVID-19 vaccines to eligible groups this winter; UKHSA advises staying home when unwell with fever. Check NHS guidance for eligibility.
rubric_hit: Watch: unusually early flu season in the US and UK; no WHO variant of concern or strained health systems

sources.title: CDC — Weekly US influenza surveillance report, week 44 ending 7 Nov 2026
Becker's Hospital Review — Flu admissions running more than 7x higher than last year

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
